summary:
WENO is an advanced geospatial intelligence platform engineered to act as a centralized spatial data administration hub for water resource management in Sub-Saharan Africa.
​By ingesting and processing core Earth observation telemetry—specifically NASA GPM/IMERG for live precipitation tracking, NASA GRACE-FO for groundwater depletion anomalies, and HLS/Landsat multispectral imagery for surface water and soil moisture indexing—WENO directly addresses the critical vulnerabilities of Sub-Saharan agricultural lands.
​For smallholder farmers and agricultural stakeholders, unpredictable rainfall and severe droughts trigger catastrophic crop failures. WENO transforms complex orbital telemetry into localized, actionable alerts. It accurately forecasts watershed stress, detects emerging drought conditions weeks in advance, and optimizes irrigation scheduling. By providing real-time hydrological visibility, the platform empowers agricultural operators to mitigate crop loss, maximize water use efficiency, and secure regional food security against climate volatility.
​Architecture Note: Engineered during the NASA Space Apps Challenge, the prototype utilizes high-fidelity synthetic datasets strictly structured on official NASA NetCDF/GeoTIFF schemas to guarantee instant scalability with live APIs.
details:
WENO — Intelligent Water Intelligence for Safe Drinking Water

1. Project Vision

WENO is an intelligent water monitoring and decision-support platform designed to improve drinking water security across Sub-Saharan Africa.

Its mission is to contribute to safer and more sustainable access to drinking water by helping communities, water utilities, NGOs, and local authorities better understand available water resources, monitor water infrastructure, and identify risks that could compromise water supply or quality.

WENO combines Earth observation data, satellite imagery, water infrastructure monitoring, water quality indicators, and artificial intelligence to transform environmental and operational data into actionable insights.

Rather than simply monitoring water resources, WENO aims to support their sustainable management and help protect the populations that depend on them.

2. A Comprehensive Approach to Drinking Water Security

WENO is built around four complementary pillars.

A. Water Availability and Resource Monitoring

Earth observation data makes it possible to monitor changes in surface water, rainfall patterns, environmental conditions, and indicators related to water resource availability.

The platform uses several satellite data sources:

  • GPM / IMERG: to monitor precipitation and identify rainfall deficits.
  • GRACE-FO: to observe large-scale variations in total water storage.
  • Landsat and Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel data: to monitor changes in surface water and surrounding environmental conditions.
  • Sentinel-2: to analyze wetlands, water bodies, and land-cover changes.

These observations help identify areas where water availability may become a concern and provide valuable context for understanding water supply challenges.

B. Drinking Water Quality Monitoring

Water quality is a central component of WENO.

The platform incorporates key physicochemical indicators used in drinking water monitoring:

  • pH;
  • turbidity;
  • residual chlorine;
  • electrical conductivity;
  • nitrates;
  • microbiological indicators, including coliform bacteria.

Measurements from IoT sensors or field inspections can be centralized to monitor water quality over time, identify unusual values, and flag situations requiring further investigation.

Water quality indicators can be presented alongside reference thresholds and recommendations from the World Health Organization (WHO).

Scientific consideration: Satellite imagery alone cannot confirm whether water from a well, borehole, or tap is safe to drink. This requires appropriate sampling and on-site testing. WENO therefore combines Earth observation with field-based monitoring to provide a more comprehensive view of drinking water security.

C. Water Infrastructure and Supply Continuity

The presence of water resources does not necessarily mean that communities can access safe drinking water. Water infrastructure plays a critical role in ensuring reliable supply.

WENO therefore considers operational information related to water points and infrastructure:

  • operational status of water points;
  • pump functionality;
  • water flow rate monitoring;
  • identification of abnormal operating conditions;
  • monitoring of service interruptions and potential supply disruptions.

By combining available information, the platform can help identify infrastructure requiring attention and prioritize maintenance activities.

D. Risk Detection and Decision Support

WENO uses data analysis and artificial intelligence to examine relationships between different indicators.

For example, declining rainfall, changes in water resource conditions, and a reduction in the flow rate of a water supply point may represent several signals that should be investigated together.

The platform can then:

  • identify potential anomalies;
  • classify alerts according to their priority;
  • display the data behind each alert;
  • suggest verification or maintenance actions;
  • generate reports for field operators and decision-makers.

The objective is to support faster, better-informed interventions before a situation becomes critical.

3. How WENO Works — Step by Step

Step 1 — Geographic Area Selection

Users select a region, hydrological basin, or area of interest. WENO displays its water-related context and available information about local water points.

Step 2 — Data Centralization

The platform brings together different categories of information, including satellite observations, rainfall data, hydrological indicators, infrastructure information, and water quality measurements.

Step 3 — Data Preparation and Structuring

Data is organized according to its source, time period, geographic location, units, and technical characteristics. Geospatial information can be handled using formats such as NetCDF and GeoTIFF.

Step 4 — Intelligent Data Analysis

Indicators are analyzed to identify unusual changes, potential risks, and situations requiring attention. Results are presented through metrics, anomaly indicators, alerts, and recommendations.

Step 5 — Interactive Monitoring and Visualization

Users access an interactive interface featuring maps, satellite observation layers, historical charts, water quality indicators, and infrastructure monitoring.

Step 6 — AI Assistance and Report Generation

The Weno-Sat assistant allows users to interact with available information, request explanations, launch certain analyses, and generate PDF reports containing indicators, alerts, and recommendations.

4. An Interface Designed to Make Data Actionable

WENO transforms complex information into an accessible monitoring environment through:

  • a water monitoring dashboard;
  • interactive mapping of geographic areas and water points;
  • satellite imagery visualization;
  • historical data comparison;
  • water quality indicators;
  • infrastructure status monitoring;
  • alerts classified by severity;
  • AI-assisted recommendations;
  • PDF reports containing charts, indicators, and summaries.

The Weno-Sat assistant, which also supports voice interaction, enables users to explore and interact with available data through a conversational interface.

5. Data Sources and Scientific Transparency

The current prototype uses simulated datasets structured to represent the formats and categories of information associated with Earth observation products, including NetCDF and GeoTIFF data structures.

The satellite missions and programs referenced by WENO — GPM, GRACE-FO, Landsat, Sentinel-2, and Harmonized Landsat-Sentinel products — represent the scientific data sources and integration pathways envisioned for the platform.

It is important to distinguish between the simulated datasets currently used to demonstrate WENO's functionality and authentic satellite observations, which will need to be integrated into a fully operational version.

The prototype architecture demonstrates the intended data workflow and provides a foundation for future connections to real data sources. Such integration will require the development and validation of appropriate data connectors, geospatial processing pipelines, and quality-control mechanisms.

6. Expected Impact

WENO aims to contribute to more proactive, transparent, and data-informed drinking water management.

Its objectives include:

  • improving visibility into water resource availability;
  • supporting the monitoring of drinking water quality indicators;
  • identifying water supply points that may require intervention;
  • helping anticipate supply disruptions and potential water quality issues;
  • facilitating coordination between water management stakeholders;
  • supporting decision-making through centralized and understandable information.

WENO — From Earth Observation to Safer Drinking Water.

A platform transforming data about our planet into actionable insights to better monitor, protect, and manage the water communities depend on.
